notes: Perfect claim overlap (C4, C39-C49). Both agree that structural data demonstrate Pol α specifically recognizes A-form RNA/DNA helix through thumb domain interactions with RNA primer backbone.

Perfect claim overlap (C5, C55, C58, C59, C78). LLM finds primer termination mechanism well-supported by structural/biochemical evidence. Peer reviewers express confusion about DNA length (~20 nt in literature vs ~10 nt in model), questioning whether structural features remain relevant for termination.

High claim overlap (C52-C54, C57). Both agree biochemical assays demonstrate Pol α preference for RNA primers and that dG-rich DNA primer experiments validate recognition of helical structure over chemical composition.

High claim overlap (C3, C25, C93-C98). Both agree crystal structures in three states are high quality and technically sound. Peer reviewers explicitly praise crystallographic work as 'impressive and technically sound.'

Moderate claim overlap (C6, C83, C84). Both rate spontaneous release mechanism as UNCERTAIN. LLM notes lack of direct evidence for release kinetics/handoff. Peer reviewers describe mechanism as 'plausible, rather than completely convincing' and request more validation.
Moderate claim overlap (C62-C66). Both agree MD simulations support induced-fit mechanism. Peer reviewers praise simulations showing polymerase requires RNA-DNA hybrid to maintain closed form.

Partial claim overlap (C7, C91). Both rate genomic stability claims as UNCERTAIN/speculative. LLM notes lack of direct evidence linking termination to reduced mutagenesis. Peer reviewers critique this as 'stated more like a fact than a possibility' and request language adjustment.

Low claim overlap (C26-C28). LLM finds ternary complex structure well-supported with appropriate documentation. Peer reviewers question whether structure truly captures 'actively copying' polymerase, asking if incorporation occurred pre-crystallization and why incoming dGTP isn't incorporated.

Minimal claim overlap (C26 only). LLM R12 addresses D998N mutant retaining activity; peer R2 questions ternary complex catalytic geometry. Related to same structure but different aspects of the claim.
Claims C69-C72 (palm domain rotation) only evaluated by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found for these structural observations about conformational changes.
Claims C73-C74 (ratchet translocation mechanism) only evaluated by LLM as highly speculative. No corresponding peer review assessment found.
Claims C37-C38 (non-crystallographic interface with acidic loop) only evaluated by LLM. Physiological relevance unclear per authors themselves. No peer review assessment found.
Claims C50-C51 (G1116E mutation and mating-type switching) only evaluated by LLM as speculative. No corresponding peer review assessment found.
